items.title: Licensed Project Review
items.caption: Landing Page Hero
items.prompt:
Create one polished business visual review image for the prompt family: Licensed Project Review.
Service anchor: FairLend Landing Page Hero Synthesis.
Service facts to preserve: Business context:
FairLend is a Canadian brokerage and investment company serving builder/developer borrowers, private mortgage clients, and investors. The hero needs to preserve the corporate/brokerage trust of the broader FairLend page while importing the higher-converting project-review flow from the build-financing page.

Source page strengths to integrate:
- Page 1 communicates company category, licensed brokerage posture, Canadian real-estate credibility, transparent terms, and technology-led underwriting.
- Page 1 uses a premium editorial split: large FairLend identity, deep green serif headline, beige background, realistic Canadian multiplex/urban housing imagery, blueprint overlay, and a license/business proof card.
- Page 2 converts builders/developers with a focused build-financing promise: "Build financing that moves with the work", progress-based reimbursement draws, no-credit-check/no-documents-required/2-minute chips, Step 1 of 7 progress stepper, blueprint-to-completed-building metaphor, and primary "Start project review" CTA with secondary "I'm just exploring".

Audience:
Canadian builders, developers, borrower/operators, and real-estate investors who need construction draw financing but also need to trust FairLend as a licensed brokerage and investment company.

Brand and layout constraints:
- Preserve FairLend's deep forest green, warm off-white/beige, restrained coral conversion accent, editorial serif headline feel, squared/low-radius premium UI, and blueprint/construction visual language.
- Use the FAiRLEND/FairLend brokerage identity as a brand cue, but do not rely on exact generated text fidelity.
- Include one clear primary conversion path for builders/developers and one quieter investor/company proof cue.
- Integrate license/proof/underwriting signals without burying the project-review CTA.
- Each output must be one unique desktop landing page hero mockup, not a collage, mood board, contact sheet, grid of pages, or multi-screen presentation.
- Keep UI text sparse and large enough to appear plausible. Avoid dense paragraphs, fake awards, discount language, mortgage-rate claims, unverified statistics, competitor logos, or unreadable microcopy.
The visual must be clearly about this service and should not introduce another brand, service, or category.
Family intent: Lead with the conversion quiz, but flank it with brokerage licensing and corporate proof so the two-minute review feels credible.
Business goal: Increase builder starts without losing the trust created by the brokerage/company page..
Scene: A polished desktop landing-page hero screenshot for FairLend: warm off-white page, full top navigation, large editorial serif headline on the left, a compact Step 1 of 7 project-review module near the CTA, and a right-side Canadian multiplex construction image with a translucent licensed brokerage proof card..
Focus: Primary focus is the builder/developer starting a project review, with secondary focus on licensed brokerage legitimacy..
Decision being supported: Can the homepage become a company-trust hero and a builder conversion entry point at once?.
Include: single desktop website hero mockup, FairLend-style nav and wordmark, large serif headline about build financing and fair lending, Step 1 of 7 progress pill, three friction-reduction chips, primary coral project-review CTA, licensed brokerage proof card, Canadian multiplex construction/blueprint visual.
Constraints: one unique hero page only, no collage, no multiple thumbnails, no mood board; premium brokerage aesthetic, low-radius UI, clean whitespace; conversion elements must be prominent but not gimmicky; generated text should be sparse and approximate, final text can be rebuilt later; keep text sparse; use short labels, UI placeholder blocks, or visual markers only when needed; keep the service moment recognizable.
Avoid: contact sheets, page grids, generic SaaS dashboard, fake awards, fake rates, fake partner marks, discount framing, overly rounded cartoon UI; fake endorsements; unsupported claims; misspelled large text; watermarks; clutter; other brands.
